description: Refactor ClusterPopup carousel from native-scroll to fully GSAP-driven transform-based carousel with Apple-style momentum drag, two-tap interaction, infinite loop, and scale+opacity effects

userStories.title: Core GSAP carousel engine with infinite loop and scale/opacity
userStories.description: As a developer, I want to replace the native-scroll carousel with a GSAP-driven transform system that positions cards via translateX, supports infinite looping via modular arithmetic, and applies scale+opacity effects based on distance from center.
acceptanceCriteria: Remove all native scroll: no overflow-x scroll/auto, no scrollLeft, no onScroll handler
Container uses overflow: hidden
Maintain a currentIndex ref (floating-point number) as the single source of truth for carousel position
Render enough cards to fill viewport + buffer (minimum 7 visible slots: 3 left + center + 3 right)
Each card positioned via transform: translateX(...) computed as (slotIndex - currentIndex) * (cardWidth + gap)
Infinite wrap: card data resolved from groups array using ((index % length) + length) % length
Center card: scale(1.05), opacity: 1. Edge cards scale down to ~0.75, opacity ~0.7
Scale/opacity updates run per-frame via GSAP onUpdate or quickSetter — compositor properties only (transform + opacity)
Cards use position: absolute within the container
Centered card has higher z-index than surrounding cards
On mount: scroll to middle of groups, call updateCardPositions to render initial state
GSAP context used for all tweens, reverted on unmount
GroupCard component is unchanged — same props, same JSX
ClusterPopupProps interface is unchanged — no breaking changes to parent
npm run type-check passes
npm run build succeeds
userStories.notes: This is the foundational story. All card positioning, wrapping, and visual effects live here. Use useRef for currentIndex, cardWidth, containerWidth — NOT React state (avoids re-renders per frame). Card width is 300px, gap is 16px. Use gsap.quickSetter for high-perf per-frame updates during drag. The extendedGroups (5x repeat) approach can be kept OR replaced with modular-index virtual rendering — either approach is fine as long as wrapping is seamless.

userStories.title: Momentum-based drag interaction with pointer events
userStories.description: As a user, I want to drag the carousel with my mouse or finger and have it respond with natural momentum and deceleration that snaps to the nearest card.
acceptanceCriteria: Use onPointerDown/onPointerMove/onPointerUp for unified mouse+touch handling
Pointer down starts tracking: record startX and current currentIndex
During drag: update currentIndex proportionally to pointer deltaX (1:1 feel with card width), update card positions per-frame
Track last 3-5 pointer positions with timestamps for velocity calculation
On pointer up: compute velocity from tracked positions
Animate currentIndex to nearest integer using gsap.to() with duration based on velocity magnitude (faster flick = further travel + longer duration)
Custom momentum: calculate target index as Math.round(currentIndex + velocity * dampingFactor), then tween to it with power2.out ease
Drag threshold: pointer movements < 5px are treated as clicks, not drags
Cursor shows grab (idle) and grabbing (dragging) states
Kill any existing snap/scroll tween before starting a new drag
Scale/opacity effects update during drag via GSAP onUpdate
npm run type-check passes
npm run build succeeds
userStories.notes: Depends on US-001 for the currentIndex system and updateCardPositions function. Velocity tracking: store [{x, t}] for last 5 pointer moves. On release: velocity = (last.x - first.x) / (last.t - first.t). Damping factor ~0.3-0.5. Duration = Math.min(0.8, Math.abs(velocity) * 0.15 + 0.3). No InertiaPlugin needed.

userStories.title: Two-tap card interaction (click to center, click to navigate)
userStories.description: As a user, I want to tap a non-centered card to snap it to center, then tap the centered card again to navigate to its group profile page.
acceptanceCriteria: Clicking a non-centered card animates currentIndex to that card's logical index with gsap.to (power2.out, ~0.5s)
Clicking the already-centered card (nearest to currentIndex) triggers onNavigate('/groups/${groupId}')
Drag movements > 5px suppress click behavior (use dragDistance tracking from US-002)
View profile button on any card still works as direct navigation (pointer-events-auto, stopPropagation)
Determine 'centered' by checking if card's logical index matches Math.round(currentIndex)
npm run type-check passes
npm run build succeeds
Verify in browser using dev-browser skill
userStories.notes: Depends on US-001 (positioning) and US-002 (drag threshold). The click handler receives the card's logical index. Compare Math.round(currentIndex.current) === cardLogicalIndex to determine if it's centered. If not centered → tween to it. If centered → navigate.

userStories.title: Keyboard navigation and accessibility
userStories.description: As a user, I want to use arrow keys to navigate the carousel and Escape to close, maintaining full keyboard accessibility.
acceptanceCriteria: Left arrow key decrements currentIndex by 1 with GSAP snap animation (power2.out, 0.4s)
Right arrow key increments currentIndex by 1 with GSAP snap animation
Escape key calls onClose
Enter or Space on the carousel triggers onNavigate for the centered card
Close button receives focus on mount
Container has role='region', aria-roledescription='carousel', appropriate aria-label
Container is focusable (tabIndex={0}) for keyboard events
npm run type-check passes
npm run build succeeds
userStories.notes: Depends on US-001 (currentIndex tween system). Reuses the same gsap.to(currentIndex, ...) pattern. Arrow keys kill any active tween before starting a new one.

userStories.title: Entry and exit animations
userStories.description: As a user, I want the carousel to animate in smoothly when appearing and animate out when closing for a polished feel.
acceptanceCriteria: On mount: container fades in (opacity 0→1) + scales from 0.9→1.0 with back.out(1.7) ease (~0.3s)
Cards stagger in from below with slight delay between each visible card
On close: reverse animation (fade out + scale down ~0.2s) THEN call onClose
Close button click and Escape key both trigger exit animation before unmounting
Use a local handleClose function that runs exit tween, then calls props.onClose in onComplete
All GSAP contexts cleaned up on unmount via gsap.context().revert()
npm run type-check passes
npm run build succeeds
Verify in browser using dev-browser skill
userStories.notes: Depends on US-001 (GSAP context setup). The exit animation means onClose is NOT called immediately — the tween's onComplete calls it. This requires changing the close button and Escape handler to use the new handleClose. Entry stagger: gsap.fromTo each visible card with y: 20 → 0, stagger: 0.05.
